stories.title: ‘Who asked that? You should be ashamed of yourself!’: Judi Dench answers questions from Ian McKellen, Lorraine Kelly, David Hare and more
stories.body: Fans and famous friends put their nosiest questions to the 91-year-old actor It’s mid-afternoon and Judi Dench and I are sitting in the “den” of her country house in Surrey. It’s one of the smallest rooms in her Elizabethan home: timber beams, terracotta-painted walls, her father’s consulting-room desk and chair within touching distance, together with the bronze “Dr Dench” plaque that used to hang on the railings outside their family home in York. Behind Judi’s head hangs an enormous painting of her as M, presented as a gift on her last day of filming on Skyfall . Through the latticed windows is a view on to the garden, which is crowded with trees she plants for lost friends and family – a beloved oak, a tribute to her late husband, actor Michael Williams, towers above the pond. Even though the room is suffused with autumn sunshine, all the lights are on in the house. Judi has always needed light around her – she’s been afraid of the dark since she was small. stories.title: USWNT seal Women’s World Cup qualification with 8-0 win over El Salvador
stories.body: US goes up 7-0 over El Salvador by half-time Win secures spot at 2027 World Cup and 2028 Olympics The United States’ place at a Women’s World Cup is treated as a foregone conclusion, but Friday’s all-or-nothing qualifier against El Salvador gave some reason for nerves. This was the first competitive game for Emma Hayes’ team since their Olympic gold medal match in August 2024, the end of two years of only friendlies. Given the global advances in women’s soccer over the years, maybe El Salvador could spring an all-time upset. The suspense ultimately lasted for eight minutes and 20 seconds. The USWNT opened the scoring in their Concacaf W Championship quarter-final with El Salvador in the ninth minute; a nifty training-ground set piece routine ending with Kennedy Wesley prodding the ball into the net, putting the hosts in the driver’s seat for an 8-0 win and a spot in next summer’s big show. With the win, the US maintains their perfect Women’s World Cup attendance record, a part of all 10 tournaments to date. Continue reading...
